body.statement: Over a field of characteristic zero, there is a probabilistic lifting-fiber algorithm which, for arbitrary polynomial equations \(f_1=\cdots=f_s=0\) and an inequation \(g\neq0\) given by a straight-line program, computes the equidimensional decomposition of the Zariski closure of their solution set. On successful generic choices the components are encoded by lifting fibers, and the arithmetic complexity is polynomial in the straight-line-program length and the intermediate geometric-degree parameter appearing in the theorem.

attestation.note: The theorem was checked for its characteristic-zero input, equations-and-inequation scope, lifting-fiber output, probabilistic success qualification, and dependence on straight-line-program length and intermediate geometric degree.
